title: Finite type relation kernels in an extension of coherent modules
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For every open $U\subseteq X$, every integer $n\geq0$ and every morphism $g:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F_2|_U$, the sheaf $\operatorname{Ker}g$ is of finite type, meaning locally generated by finitely many sections.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), proof of (4), relation-kernel diagram

proof.text: Restrict the short exact sequence to U. Restrictions preserve exactness: the local lifting conditions for opens contained in U are unchanged. Compose g with the last map and let K3 be its kernel. Coherence restricts to U by applying the same finite-generator and relation conditions on opens of U, which are opens of X. Thus K3 is finite type by coherence of the last term.

The map K3 to the middle term lands in the first term because its composite into the last term is zero. The universal property of a short exact kernel supplies this map. Its kernel is the kernel of g: equivalently the snake lemma applied to the top row zero-free-free with identity gives the exact sequence zero-kernel g-K3-first.

The first term restricted to U is coherent, again directly from the open-local definition. The kernel of a map from the finite type K3 to this coherent first term is finite type by the finite type kernel lemma. Transport along the kernel identification from the preceding step.
